items.text: AP via ABC7/PBS/Yahoo, Washington Times (June 11): Trump opened Thursday by threatening the US would hit Iran 'VERY HARD TONIGHT' and take 'total control' of Iran's oil and gas industries, including the Kharg Island export terminal — a major supply-shock threat that pushed Brent to $93.5. Hours later, Trump posted on Truth Social that discussions with Iran 'have been brought to the highest level of Iranian leadership and approved,' and that he had 'cancelled the scheduled strikes.' In an Oval Office event, Trump declared: 'We just made a great settlement of the war with Iran,' offering scant details beyond expecting the ceasefire-extension agreement to be finalized 'over the next few days.' This is the sharpest reversal of the entire 104-day conflict — from imminent major escalation to claimed 'settlement' within hours.

items.bold: CONTRADICTION: Iran FM spokesperson says deal 'mostly finalized' but blames US 'contradictions' for turbulence. A senior Iranian official told MS NOW Iran has NOT YET AGREED to any MOU — directly disputing Trump's 'great settlement' claim.
items.text: ABC7/AP (June 11), MS NOW live (June 11, 9:52 PM EDT): Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said on Iranian state television that the text of a deal is 'mostly finalized,' but added: 'The problem is that the contradictions in America's position has caused turbulence to this process.' However, a senior Iranian official linked to the talks told MS NOW that Iran has NOT YET agreed to any memorandum of understanding or framework of a deal with the United States — a direct contradiction of Trump's framing. This gap between Trump's triumphant 'great settlement' language and Iran's more guarded 'mostly finalized but not yet agreed' position is the central uncertainty heading into Friday. The pattern matches previous false dawns (Day 86 'largely negotiated', Day 99 'pretty close') — but this time accompanied by an actual cancellation of imminent strikes and a 3.6% Brent crash, suggesting markets see this iteration as more credible.

items.text: Reuters/Investing.com (June 11): Brent futures fell $3.37, or 3.6%, to $89.73 a barrel by 1:38 PM EDT, while WTI fell $3.20 (3.6%) to $86.83. This was a direct market reaction to Trump's strike cancellation — the sharpest single-event Brent decline since the original April 8 ceasefire announcement (which saw a ~16% one-day drop). Earlier Thursday, Brent had climbed to $93.5 after Trump's threat to seize 'total control' of Iran's oil infrastructure including Kharg Island — a threat that, if executed, would represent the most severe supply-side escalation of the war (Kharg Island handles ~90% of Iran's oil exports). The whipsaw from $93.5 to $89.73 within a single session — a $3.77 swing — illustrates how tightly oil markets are now tracking Trump's individual statements rather than ground-truth military developments.

items.text: CBS News live updates (June 10): At a UN Security Council meeting on the Middle East, Secretary-General António Guterres warned: 'We should not minimize the risks of a lesser fire becoming full fire, or in another word – full war.' UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk added: 'We have, I mean, we're always very relieved when ceasefires are announced, but ceasefires need to be respected in full... I was horrified by the fact that we see escalation upon escalation.' This came after Iran attacked American bases in Jordan and Bahrain on Wednesday in retaliation for the US strikes that followed the Apache helicopter downing. The IDF separately said it killed 20 Hezbollah fighters in southern Lebanon over the past two weeks despite the Lebanon-Israel ceasefire extension signed in Washington last week — confirming the Lebanon front remains active even as the main US-Iran track shows signs of a possible breakthrough.

military.t: TRUMP CANCELLED PLANNED 'VERY HARD' STRIKES on Iran — Claims 'Great Settlement of the War.' Hours Earlier Threatened 'Total Control' of Iran's Oil Industry Including Kharg Island. Brent Crashed -3.6%.
military.d: AP via PBS/ABC7/Yahoo, Washington Times (June 11): Thursday began with Trump threatening the most severe escalation of the war — hitting Iran 'VERY HARD TONIGHT' and seizing 'total control' of Iran's oil and gas industries, including the Kharg Island terminal that handles roughly 90% of Iran's oil exports. Brent spiked to $93.5 on the threat. Hours later, Trump reversed entirely: 'Based on the fact that discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran have been brought to the highest level of Iranian leadership and approved, I have... cancelled the scheduled strikes.' In the Oval Office: 'We just made a great settlement of the war with Iran.' He offered no details beyond expecting the ceasefire-extension deal to be finalized 'over the next few days.' Brent crashed -3.6% ($3.37) to $89.73 — the biggest single-event drop since the original April 8 ceasefire (~16% one-day drop). The whipsaw — from imminent seizure of Iran's oil infrastructure to a claimed 'great settlement' within hours — is unprecedented even by this conflict's volatile standards.

military.t: IRAN'S RESPONSE IS MIXED: FM Spokesperson Says Deal 'Mostly Finalized' but US 'Contradictions' Cause 'Turbulence.' Senior Iranian Official Tells MS NOW: NO MOU AGREED YET — Directly Disputes Trump.
military.d: ABC7/AP (June 11), MS NOW live (9:52 PM EDT June 11): Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei told Iranian state television the text of a deal is 'mostly finalized' — but added pointedly: 'The problem is that the contradictions in America's position has caused turbulence to this process.' Separately and more starkly, a senior Iranian official linked to the talks told MS NOW that Iran has NOT YET agreed to any memorandum of understanding or framework of a deal with the United States — a direct contradiction of Trump's 'great settlement' framing. The Qatari delegation that departed Tehran Thursday morning after overnight talks was characterised by a source as having achieved 'breakthroughs' with the deal 'very close' — a more measured assessment than either Trump's triumphalism or the senior Iranian official's flat denial. The pattern echoes prior false-dawn moments (Day 86 'largely negotiated', Day 99 'pretty close', Day 101 'final objective just about to be achieved') — but this time accompanied by an actual cancellation of imminent major strikes and a real 3.6% Brent crash, which markets evidently found at least partially credible.

military.t: UN SECRETARY-GENERAL GUTERRES: Risk of 'FULL WAR' — 'A Lesser Fire Becoming Full Fire.' UN Rights Chief 'Horrified.' Iran Attacked US Bases in Jordan + Bahrain Wednesday. IDF Killed 20 Hezbollah Fighters Despite Ceasefire.
military.d: CBS News live updates (June 10): At a UN Security Council session on the Middle East, Secretary-General António Guterres delivered a stark warning: 'We should not minimize the risks of a lesser fire becoming full fire, or in another word – full war.' UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk added: 'We have, I mean, we're always very relieved when ceasefires are announced, but ceasefires need to be respected in full... I was horrified by the fact that we see escalation upon escalation.' This came after Iran attacked American bases in Jordan and Bahrain Wednesday — retaliation for the US strikes that followed the Apache helicopter downing earlier in the week. Separately, the IDF said its 'Shahaf' unit had killed 20 Hezbollah fighters in southern Lebanon over the prior two weeks, working in cooperation with the Israeli Air Force to strike Hezbollah drone-launch infrastructure — despite the Lebanon-Israel ceasefire extension signed in Washington just last week. The UN's framing — international institutions now openly worried about 'full war' even as Trump claims a 'great settlement' — captures the extraordinary range of assessments circulating about this conflict's trajectory as of Friday morning.

assessment.body:
Friday 7:30 AM IST. Day 104.
The wildest 24 hours of a 104-day war.

THE MORNING THREAT
Trump: US will hit Iran "VERY HARD TONIGHT."
Trump: US will take "total control" of Iran's oil and gas industry —
including Kharg Island, which handles ~90% of Iran's oil exports.
This would have been the most severe supply-side escalation of the war.
Brent spiked to $93.5.

THE EVENING REVERSAL
Hours later, Trump cancelled the strikes entirely.
Truth Social: discussions "brought to the highest level of Iranian
leadership and approved." Strikes "cancelled."
Oval Office: "We just made a great settlement of the war with Iran."
Expects the ceasefire-extension deal finalized "over the next few days."

THE MARKET BELIEVED IT — PARTIALLY
Brent crashed -3.6% ($3.37) to $89.73. WTI to $86.83.
Biggest single-event oil drop since the April 8 ceasefire.
A $3.77 swing within one session — from $93.5 to $89.73.

BUT IRAN'S STORY DOESN'T MATCH
FM spokesperson Baghaei: deal "mostly finalized" but US
"contradictions" causing "turbulence."
A SENIOR IRANIAN OFFICIAL told MS NOW: Iran has NOT YET
agreed to any MOU or framework. Period.
This directly contradicts "great settlement of the war."

THE WIDER CONTEXT — SOMEHOW, SAME WEEK
UN Sec-Gen Guterres: risk of "a lesser fire becoming full fire... full war."
UN rights chief: "horrified... escalation upon escalation."
Iran attacked US bases in Jordan + Bahrain Wednesday.
IDF killed 20 Hezbollah fighters in 2 weeks — Lebanon ceasefire strained.
World Bank cut global growth forecast. ECB raised rates.
US producer prices: biggest jump since 2022.
Yet: UAE-Iran held rare direct talks. Qatari mediators say "breakthroughs."

WHERE THIS LEAVES INDIA
Nifty Thursday close 23,162 (-0.23%) — entirely PRE-CANCELLATION.
Friday's open is the single most consequential of the 104-day war:
- If Brent holds near $89-90 and Iran doesn't formally deny →
  relief rally, Nifty could test 23,400-23,500.
- If Iran's "no MOU yet" hardens into a formal denial →
  Brent rebounds toward $93+, Nifty risk returns to 23,000-23,100.
The MT Settebello tragedy (3 Indian deaths) remains a live
India-US diplomatic issue, independent of this whiplash —
G7 (June 15-17) looms as the next major checkpoint.
Watch GIFT Nifty and Brent's Asian-session open above all else.
